degenerate

/dih-JEN-uh-rayt/ — the verb ends like 'crate'; the adjective ends like 'it' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Degenerate means to sink into a worse or lower state — to lose the quality or character that made something what it was.

Without its moderator the neighborhood forum degenerated in a single winter, careful book threads giving way to feuds and spam.

Example

The Riverside Sunday softball league was founded for families — lawn chairs, juice boxes, a rule that everybody bats. By its third summer it had degenerated past recognizing: hired ringers in matching cleats, a bench-clearing argument over a checked swing, and at last a lawyer's letter, on real letterhead, disputing the strike zone.

Degenerate is the exact verb because the league did not simply get shabbier — it sank into a lower kind of thing, a feud wearing uniforms. Its unit-mate deteriorate covers the field's fate that same summer: weeds, a sagging backstop, a condition running down while the field stayed a field. When a thing's character falls, it degenerates; when its condition wears, it deteriorates.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

decay: Decay is physical rot — teeth, timber, fallen fruit breaking down into ruin. Degenerate is broader and aims at character: a debate, a league, or a friendship degenerates when it slides into a lower version of itself, no rot required.

regress: Regress means to slip back to an earlier stage: a patient regresses, a skill regresses under stress. It measures backward motion and says nothing about quality. Degenerate adds the fall: what comes out the far end is not just earlier but worse.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

improve: to change for the better — the plain opposite

flourish: to grow strong and thriving instead of sinking

Where it sits · how much of the original character survives

worsen → degenerate → disintegrate

worsen vs. degenerate: Worsen is weaker than degenerate: a worsening debate grows testier but is still a debate, while a degenerating one is sliding into something lower — a shouting match that has stopped being debate at all.

disintegrate vs. degenerate: Disintegrate goes further than degenerate: a degenerated league has sunk into a worse version of itself, but a league that disintegrates comes apart completely, leaving nothing whole enough to have a character at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-: down, away from

Root — gener: kind, birth, origin (Latin genus)

Suffix — -ate: to make or become

Put it together: De- (down, away from) + gener (kind, birth, origin — Latin genus) + -ate (to become) = to fall away from one's kind. The Romans meant it almost genealogically: to become unworthy of one's ancestors. English kept the picture of a fall from origin — whatever degenerates is measured against the better thing it used to be. The gener- family is everywhere: generate, generation, genre, generous.

Use the root in a new word: regenerate: Her favorite chapter in the biology text is the one on how flatworms regenerate.

Root Check

Word Choice

negative / judging

Degenerate is the harsher verdict in this unit: it says a thing has sunk into a lower kind of itself — a debate into a brawl, a hobby into a feud. Its unit-mate deteriorate tracks a condition running down while the thing stays what it is: roads, eyesight, and friendships deteriorate. And note the shift when the word turns adjective or noun (/dih-JEN-er-it/): applied to a person it is openly contemptuous. The SAT wants the verb.
